EVERETT, Washington, Nov 15 : Three-time world champion Ilia Malinin claimed the Skate America title in Everett on Saturday, winning the event for a fourth time and delighting audiences with a choreo spin inspired by his mother. It marked a successful start to a campaign in which Malinin is seeking to balance the technical difficulty he is known for with greater artistic expression. The American finished with a total score of 284.31 points after topping the short program on Friday and placing second in the free skate, securing victory by 9.58 points over Italy's Daniel Grassl. Grassl produced the strongest free skate of the event, climbing from fourth after the short program to finish with 274.73, while Israel's Tamir Kuperman completed the podium on with 248.55 in his senior Grand Prix debut.

Performing his "Blue Eye Samurai" free skate, Malinin overcame a slightly awkward landing on his opening quad flip before nailing a triple Axel and quad toe loop. The 21-year-old, nicknamed the "Quad God", then landed a quad Lutz-triple Axel-double Axel combination, adding a triple Lutz-double toe loop and a quad Salchow before bringing the crowd to its feet with his trademark backflip. He opted against attempting his signature quadruple Axel, instead delighting the crowd with a choreo spin. "It was definitely the most fun I've ever had, but skating that program, man, I'm tired," Malinin told NBC. "My legs, at the end of the program, just nearly gave up on me, but I'm glad I was able to stay on my feet most of the time, and I'm just looking forward to how the program progresses in the future." Malinin said his mother Tatiana Malinina, the 1999 Grand Prix Final champion, was a constant source of inspiration. "She's been there for me ever since I was born, and I always appreciate everything she does for me," he said. Malinin had a roller-coaster 2025-26 season. He saw his 14-event winning streak end at the Winter Olympics, where he finished eighth in the singles event, before rebounding weeks later to capture a third consecutive world title. Malinin will return to action at the NHK Trophy in Japan in two weeks, where a podium finish is expected to secure his place at December's Grand Prix Final, an event he has won in each of the last three seasons.

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Nov 15 : American Kayla Harrison leveraged her tremendous grappling skills to snatch a fourth-round submission win over Amanda Nunes on Saturday night as she retained her UFC bantamweight title, thwarting her opponent's attempt to take the belt back after more than three years out of the cage.  In the main event at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden, Ciryl Gane of France defeated American Josh Hokit by unanimous decision to retain the heavyweight title after a bruising five-round battle fought at a frenetic pace.  A two-time Olympic judo champion, the 36-year-old Harrison was facing arguably the greatest female fighter of all time in Nunes, a dominant two-weight champion at bantamweight and featherweight before she stepped away from the sport in June 2023. But the Brazilian could not shake off the rust of her long absence as she let the fight slip away from her.  Nunes did well initially, looking crisp in her striking and avoiding some early takedown attempts, but she eventually succumbed to Harrison's grappling attack, spending much of the latter part of the opening two rounds on the bottom in a scarf-hold position from which she struggled to escape.

In the fourth round, she chased Nunes down to the mat, jumping on her back and quickly sinking in a rear-naked choke that forced the 38-year-old to submit.  “I think I’m still in shock,” said Harrison, who had surgery on herniated disks in her neck in January.  “It feels surreal. Sometimes I can’t believe my life. I’m just really grateful, I’m humble, it’s an honour and a privilege to stand before you."

Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday (Nov 15), its first such warnings since September, as Iran said it had attacked a US base in the Gulf country amid uncertainty over a US-Iran deal aimed at ending the nearly nine-month-old war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had attacked a US military base in Bahrain in retaliation for "hostile US actions", Iran's Fars news agency reported. The Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air-defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in Bahrain, Iranian state-run Press TV reported. There was no immediate confirmation from US or Bahraini authorities. Bahrain, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, urged citizens and residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, the interior ministry said. It did not provide further details on the threats.

Two days earlier the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain . The US military denied this, saying it had intercepted two Iranian drones without any damage. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, though Washington and Tehran have held off on direct attacks in the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28 and then spread across the region, with Tehran launching missile and drone attacks on US bases in Gulf countries. President Donald Trump has said in recent days that he might hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, but that he would maintain a US naval blockade, Reuters reported on Saturday. On another front, however, the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition fighting them have continued to exchange attacks, with the coalition saying on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province.

JERUSALEM: The Israeli military said on Sunday (Nov 15) its forces had struck a senior militant from Hamas's military wing, which confirmed the death of one of its commanders in Gaza. Samir Abu Younis, a military leader who played a key role in planning Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel, was killed on Saturday, according to a statement from the Islamist movement's Al-Qassam Brigade. "A short while ago, the IDF and ISA struck a senior terrorist in Hamas' military wing," the Israeli military said in a joint statement with internal security agency Shin Bet, in the early hours of Sunday morning. It did not elaborate but said it would later provide further details. "He was killed yesterday evening ... in a cowardly assassination operation," the Al-Qassam Brigade posted on Telegram, adding Younis was "among the most important commanders involved in the planning and supervision of the Oct 7 attack". A security source told AFP shortly after midnight that Younis, the commander of Al-Qassam's Rafah Brigade, died in a strike "targeting him moments ago in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis." Gaza's civil defence spokesman, Mahmoud Bassal, told AFP the agency had received the body of Younis, 53, and said two people were wounded in the strike in Gaza's south. Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by the Oct 7 attack. While the US-backed ceasefire has largely subdued the fighting, Israel has kept up regular strikes in the territory. More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations. During the same period, the Israeli military has reported the loss of seven soldiers, as well as one civilian contractor. Israel's former army chief Gadi Eisenkot is currently locked in negotiations to form a governing coalition while his rival, caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, remains responsible for military operations.

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Aryna Sabalenka apologised on Saturday for her angry outburst during her defeat by Ukraine's Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals. Television footage appeared to show the Belarusian swearing during Friday's round-robin match, with some social media users interpreting her remarks as being directed at Svitolina or Ukrainians. The loss eliminated Sabalenka from the season-ending tournament. "My comment was not directed at Elina," Sabalenka said in a social media post. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

Svitolina did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian or Belarusian opponents following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which Moscow launched with Belarus as a staging ground.  Asked about her reaction to Sabalenka's apology, Svitolina called for mutual respect, acknowledging that fans' passions can sometimes run high. "We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans, I have my fans," she told reporters after her semi-final win over Linda Noskova on Saturday. She expressed hope that matches between the two of them would be respected, "because yes, sometimes in some matches that we've played, also been not great comments towards me in regards of the war." Svitolina, the 2018 WTA Finals champion, faces Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in Sunday's final.

DUBLIN, Nov 14 : Ireland secured an emphatic 43-15 victory over Fiji in the Nations Championship on Saturday to stay in contention for a place in the final of the new competition. Ireland were 17-15 ahead at halftime and stretched their lead after the break to move to 20 points in the Northern Hemisphere standings, level with England and a point behind France. Wingers Tommy O’Brien and Robert Baloucoune scored two tries each with Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and Nick Tominey getting the other three. Fiji’s two tries came with four minutes midway through the first half from Josua Tuisova and captain Peceli Yato.

Ireland were wary of the danger of another upset in the Nations Championship after New Zealand and South Africa were beaten this weekend, but O’Brien went over in the eighth minute to settle their nerves. Fiji’s double strike put them 12-7 ahead, however, before right wing Baloucoune went over twice in the last 10 minutes of the first half. Ben Volavola’s penalty on the stroke of halftime reduced Ireland’s lead to two points but after the interval the gulf in quality became more apparent. Ireland stretched their lead when Kelleher scored from a lineout maul and Porter placed the ball over the line from a simple tap-and-go. Fiji’s desperation to stay in the contest led to many mistakes and Ireland took advantage in the 59th minute as Sam Prendergast sent a superb grubber kick through for O’Brien to pounce on before Timoney completed the rout. Ireland must now beat South Africa and hope France, who host Argentina, and England, who take on New Zealand, falter in Saturday’s matches to secure a place in the final at Twickenham on November 29. BRAGA, Portugal, Nov 14 : Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement ended in a crushing 4-1 home defeat by Denmark in the Nations League on Saturday, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice as a night of tributes in Braga turned sour for Jorge Jesus and his players. Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo in the other League A Group Four match, with Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup scoring before Erling Haaland's late penalty sealed victory. Portugal remain top on 12 points, three ahead of Denmark, with Norway third on six and Wales bottom on three. One round of league-phase matches remains, with Wales hosting Portugal and Denmark at home to Norway on Tuesday. In front of a packed stadium, Portugal's players wore shirts bearing Ronaldo's name and number seven during the national anthem.

Supporters unfurled a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão" — "Thank you, captain" — alongside images of him lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies. Ronaldo announced his international retirement on social media last week following a public falling-out with manager Jesus. DENMARK RUN RIOT Portugal dominated much of the first half in pouring rain but fell behind shortly before halftime. Hojlund had a header ruled out for a foul by Joachim Andersen in the build-up before another aerial effort struck Ruben Dias’ hand. Following a VAR intervention and pitchside review, the referee awarded a penalty which Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg drove into the top-right corner shortly before halftime. Hojlund doubled Denmark's advantage five minutes after the interval, slipping behind the defence to meet a cross from the right with a powerful volley. The striker scored again seven minutes later, cutting inside Renato Veiga on a counter-attack before firing a right-footed shot past Diogo Costa from the edge of the box. Andersen completed the rout in the 75th minute, rising to power home a towering header from i.nside the area after Mathias Jensen delivered a free kick from the right. Bernardo Silva scored a consolation goal for Portugal three minutes into added time, firing home from close range after the goalkeeper parried the ball. “Practically everything went wrong for us... It’s actually hard to find an explanation," midfielder Joao Palhinha told Portuguese broadcaster Sport TV.  "It was an unlucky night for us; we made it far too easy for our opponents. We’ve got a match on Tuesday, so we’ve got until then to reflect about what happened today. But I have no doubt whatsoever that we’ll bounce back and secure top spot in the group in Wales.” NORWAY PUNISH WALES After a subdued first half at Ullevaal Stadion, Nusa broke the deadlock in the 59th minute with a half-volley from the edge of the area following a partially cleared corner. Schjelderup doubled the lead two minutes after coming off the bench. Nusa raced down the left and fed Haaland, who squared for the substitute to tap into an empty net at the far post. David Brooks gave Wales hope in the 79th minute, racing onto a through ball and chipping the advancing goalkeeper despite pressure from a defender. But Connor Roberts fouled Schjelderup inside the area six minutes later and Haaland converted the resulting penalty in the 88th minute to secure Norway's win.

Source: Reuters

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva extended her unbeaten run at the WTA Finals on Saturday, dispatching American Jessica Pegula 6-3 6-4 to reach the final, where she will face a resurgent Elina Svitolina. Andreeva's heavy groundstrokes, strong serving and tireless defense were too much for the American in their first career meeting, played under sunny skies in the California desert. "It was a tough match," Andreeva said. "You have to work hard to win a point against her. She is going to leave everything out there and make your life complicated, so I wanted to make her life complicated as well today." The opening set was tight until Andreeva pounced on a looping shot from Pegula and drilled a forehand winner to break serve for a 5-3 lead.

Pegula, backed by a supportive crowd, earned break points as Andreeva served for the set, but shanked an overhead and Andreeva took the set two points later when her opponent's backhand found the net. Pegula broke to grab a 3-1 advantage in the second set but the lead would prove short-lived. Andreeva broke straight back with a deft volley and broke again to lead 4-3. The tournament's third seed ultimately sealed the win when a Pegula backhand sailed long on match point. Andreeva, making her WTA Finals debut, has not dropped a set in four matches at the event. SVITOLINA SHINES She will face sixth seed Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final after the Ukrainian needed just over an hour to cruise past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in Saturday's other semi-final. Despite strong sun shining in her eyes, Svitolina delivered a crosscourt backhand winner to claim the first set. She raced out to a 5-0 lead in the second and raised her arms in triumph and beamed a smile after Noskova's forehand went wide on match point. Andreeva holds a 2-1 lead in their head-to-head matchups, including a one-sided 6-4 6-0 victory in their round-robin match on Monday, but Svitolina has raised her level since. "It's going to be another big challenge, of course, and I feel I have to do my homework," she said. "But I feel I'm a completely different player from the first match. I was not playing the right way. I will give it my best shot." Svitolina has now made the final all three times she has competed in the eight-player championships, winning it in 2018. The $10 million tournament was moved from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden because of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Source: Reuters

STARBASE, Texas: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft on Saturday (Nov 14) returned from a 22-hour voyage in orbit and descended for the first time into the grasp of giant mechanical arms at the Texas tower it was launched from a day earlier, a catch that is essential to the company's decade-long effort to develop a fully reusable rocket. The 52m Starship fell out of thick clouds over SpaceX's Starbase launch site, reignited engines to flip itself vertical and slowly descended into the tower's "Mechazilla" arms, engines still roaring. Charred from the blazing heat of its return from space, the ship shut down its engines and hung still after the rocket system's longest mission yet. "That was the missing link, the holy grail of spaceflight," SpaceX mission commentator Dan Huot said of the ship catch. The towering two-stage rocket's Super Heavy booster - the rocket's bottom half - carried Starship to space on Friday, lifting off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, facilities. That booster had failed to make a similar return to the launch pad some 10 minutes after liftoff, nixing SpaceX's plan to recover both parts of the rocket for the first time.

But the Starship upper stage's successful return after orbiting Earth 14 times for 22.5 hours marked a key engineering milestone in the whirlwind, multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees as the future workhorse for SpaceX's lucrative Starlink satellite business, as well as ambitions to put data centres in orbit, return humans to the moon and, eventually, settle on Mars.

After deploying 26 Starlink satellites in orbit Friday night while cruising some 260km in altitude, Starship on Saturday fired one of its engines to begin an atmospheric plunge while flying eastward over the Pacific Ocean. It faced blistering heat as its orbital speed of some 17,000 miles per hour slowed to a supersonic free-fall in the skies above SpaceX's Starbase facilities on the Gulf Coast of south Texas. With its aerodynamic fins folded back, two small fittings near the top of Starship hooked onto the launch tower's mechanical arms that had closed in to grasp it, allowing the vessel to hang a few hundred feet off the ground. Musk and SpaceX engineers began inspecting the ship within hours of its catch. "Ship 42 looks great!" Musk wrote on X, posting photos and videos from the launch tower. SHIP'S RETURN ADVANCES ROCKET REUSABILITY SpaceX's dominance in the global launch industry is centred on its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, which has launched over 700 times since 2010. That rocket's first stage is reusable, but its second stage - the part that delivers payloads into orbit - is discarded into the ocean after each flight. With Starship, Musk wants a rocket system that can fly to space and back in a manner and tempo akin to commercial airplanes, with minimal refurbishment between flights.

SpaceX's mega rocket Starship returns to its launch pad to be caught by the launch tower following a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Nov 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Eric Gay)

Though Saturday's Starship recovery is a key milestone in that effort, SpaceX has yet to recover both Starship stages in a single mission, which would mark the first-ever return of an orbital launch system. And Starship's heat shield, composed of hundreds of black hexagonal tiles that protect it from the blazing heat of atmospheric reentry, is itself not yet fully reusable. SpaceX is trying to engineer new tile designs that will require little to no refurbishment after each mission. NASA's Space Shuttle system that ferried astronauts to the International Space Station before its 2011 retirement was partially reusable; its external fuel tanks that got it off Earth were discarded after each flight. The reusable spacecraft itself had to go through extensive refurbishment before re-flying. SpaceX has spent more than US$15 billion on Starship's development. NASA has provided US$3.2 billion as part of a contract valued at more than US$4 billion that SpaceX won in 2021 to return humans to the moon using Starship under the space agency's Artemis program. NASA expects Starship, along with another moon lander under development by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, to start crewed flights to the moon in 2028, though several challenging development milestones remain with both mooncraft. For Starship, those milestones include demonstrating complex fuel transfers between Starship tanker rockets in orbit, a critical process that will enable the ship to travel beyond Earth's orbit to the moon.

Source: Reuters/rj/ec
